subject: Trial exit tests and ownership ledger
messages:
From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Nguyen <sara@medpilot.com>
Cc: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Trial exit tests and ownership ledger

Sara — following our call this morning, attached is a compact ownership ledger and the first draft of the trial exit tests we discussed. Goal: put clear, unambiguous acceptance criteria in the MAP so procurement and your engineering leads can sign off without back-and-forth.

High-level asks from our side:
- Confirm which of these acceptance tests MedPilot will own vs Redwood will own (column: owner).
- Prioritize tests 1–6 as you noted on the call; we'll split the rest into Phase 2.
- Confirm target pass thresholds (e.g., 95th pct latency under 250ms; mean embed similarity > 0.82).

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm ownership by EOD Wednesday (22 Jul).
2) We run the smoke test run on Thursday (23 Jul) and share results same day.
3) If all pass, we move to a short canary for 5000 requests/day next week and prepare SLA paperwork.

Attachment: trial-test-matrix.xlsx (sheet: tests, owners, thresholds)

— Lauren Bishop
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.ai | +1 415 555 0132

Redwood Inference — Production-first LLM inference

From: Sara Nguyen <sara@medpilot.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Procurement Team <procure@healthcorp.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 10:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Trial exit tests and ownership ledger

Thanks Lauren — this looks great and much clearer than the earlier doc. Quick notes from our side: 
- Ownership: MedPilot will take lead on tests 1 (response correctness sampling), 3 (privacy/PII scrub verification), and 5 (end-to-end tracing). Redwood to own 2 (latency SLO validation), 4 (KV cache behavior under warm start), and 6 (tokenization parity). I'll mark exceptions in the matrix.
- Thresholds: the latency target is doable but can we make it a rolling 30-min window at 95th pct? Our infra has bursty periods; that window aligns with our ops SLA.
- Procurement: please share the acceptance evidence template so we can attach artifacts for audit (logs, sample transcripts, smoke-run report). Procurement looped in to confirm audit trail format.

I can confirm owners by COB Wednesday (22 Jul). Can we keep the smoke window to 10:00–12:00 PT on Thursday (23 Jul)? That's our low-traffic slot.

— Sara Nguyen
Head of Product Operations, MedPilot Health
sara@medpilot.com | +1 617 555 0921

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Nguyen <sara@medpilot.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 23 Jul 2026 08:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Trial exit tests and ownership ledger

Adding the concrete test definitions and evidence checklist below (pulled from the attached matrix). I've also uploaded the test matrix to the shared drive (link in metadata).

Acceptance tests (summary):
1) Correctness spot-check (Owner: MedPilot) — 200 human-evaluated prompts, >90% pass per rubric v2. Evidence: CSV of prompts + labels, auditor notes.
2) Latency SLO (Owner: Redwood) — rolling 30-min 95th percentile < 250ms for 95% of windows during smoke. Evidence: Prometheus histogram exports + aggregated window report.
3) PII scrub verification (Owner: MedPilot) — 500 synthetic prompts containing PII templates; scrubbed tokens < 0.1% leak rate. Evidence: redacted logs and scrub test harness output.
4) KV caching warm-start behavior (Owner: Redwood) — cold vs warm comparison; warm requests must show >=2x throughput improvement without QoS degradation. Evidence: perf traces + sample KV sizes.
5) End-to-end tracing (Owner: MedPilot) — every failing request must show span linking from request to model shard; failure rate for trace gaps <0.5%. Evidence: trace ids + sample traces.
6) Tokenization parity (Owner: Redwood) — library parity tests across our quantized runtime and reference tokenizer for 10k tokens. Evidence: diff artifacts.

Run cadence and ownership ledger:
- 23 Jul 10:00–12:00 PT: smoke run (Redwood to provision test traffic; MedPilot to stand by for correctness audits).
- 24 Jul 09:00 PT: results digest and decision — go/no-go for canary.

Attachment (referenced): trial-test-matrix.xlsx — contains full thresholds and evidence checklist.

I will be on the smoke run and will push the Prometheus exports to the shared drive immediately after the window.

— Ben Carter
Sr. Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai | +1 650 555 0104

From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Nguyen <sara@medpilot.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Procurement Team <procure@healthcorp.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Jul 2026 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Trial exit tests and ownership ledger

Thanks all — appreciate the quick alignment. Sara, thanks for confirming owners and the window — 10:00–12:00 PT on Thu works for us. A couple of operational notes before we run: 

- Evidence packaging: Ben will drop a README in the drive describing the expected file names and the minimal metadata (timestamp, test-id, owner). Procurement: that README should satisfy your audit ingestion step; if not, flag the missing field and we'll iterate.
- Failure modes and remediation: For anything marked as "fail but recoverable" we'll plan a 48-hour remediation window. Major fails (security, data leakage) will trigger our escalation path and pause the trial.
- Sign-off: decision rubric is in the matrix (Pass / Conditional Pass / Fail). Conditional Pass requires a mitigation plan + timeline submitted within 48 hours.

I'll run the decision meeting on Friday 24 Jul 09:00 PT to review artifacts and the pass/fail signals. If all green, legal will kick off the SLA addendum and procurement can prepare PO steps.

See you on Thursday — I'll ping again 09:45 PT with the readiness check.

— Lauren
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.ai | +1 415 555 0132
